CHIEF COMPLAINT
Hypogonadism follow-up visit.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Paul Edwards is a 59-year-old HIV-positive male presenting for follow-up of hypogonadism. Patient reports feeling well on current testosterone replacement therapy at 1 milliliter every 10 days (140 milligrams). He describes improved energy, vigor, and sleep quality. Patient notes improved bloodwork including significant reduction in triglycerides from 265 mg/dL to 145 mg/dL over the 5 months since starting testosterone replacement. He reports his red blood cell count has increased and remains stable. Patient is currently taking finasteride 5 milligrams at half-pill dose daily. He takes cialis 5 milligrams on days he works out, otherwise 2.5 milligrams daily, though he reports recently running out. Patient requested discussion regarding possible dose increase to 175 milligrams but was counseled against this due to already elevated peak testosterone levels above 1,500. Patient inquired about indole-3-carbinol or broccoli extract for estrogen control but was advised this is not necessary given normal estradiol levels.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient reports good overall health, improved sleep, increased vigor, and good general well-being. No other concerns mentioned.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
HIV-positive.

MEDICATIONS
Testosterone replacement therapy 1 milliliter every 10 days (140 milligrams).
Finasteride 5 milligrams half-pill daily.
Cialis 2.5 to 5 milligrams daily depending on workout schedule.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Not discussed.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: Patient appears trim. Cardiovascular: Heart sounds normal, no concerns. Respiratory: Lungs clear, no concerns.

RESULTS
PSA: 0.6 ng/mL (previous 0.5 ng/mL last year).
Cholesterol and triglycerides improved significantly.
Red blood cell count increased and stable.
Estradiol: Not elevated on recent testing.
Testosterone peak levels previously greater than 1,500 ng/dL.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
59-year-old HIV-positive male with hypogonadism on testosterone replacement therapy responding well clinically and biochemically. PSA stable and well below concerning threshold. Patient counseled against dose increase to 175 milligrams due to risk of elevated peaks exceeding 1,500 ng/dL, which increases risk of polycythemia and need to discontinue therapy. Current dose of 140 milligrams maintained. Estradiol monitoring not necessary at this time given normal levels. PSA to be checked annually. Refills requested for finasteride, cialis, and testosterone. Patient prefers paper prescriptions from Walmart Pharmacy.
